# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 75 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 75 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_075_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Part 2 — The Rock, the Gate, and the Virgins

**75:1** In the middle of the plain he showed me a great white rock rising up from the plain. The rock was higher than the mountains, four-sided, so that it could accommodate the whole world. Now this rock was ancient, and had a gate cut into it; but the gate appeared to have been recently cut, for it shone more brightly than the sun.

**75:2** Around the gate stood twelve virgins. The four who stood at the corners seemed more glorious than the rest; but the others were also glorious. And they stood at the four corners of the gate, two on each side, and virgins stood on either side of the gate.

**75:3** And I said to him: "What does this gate mean?" "It is the Son of God," he said to me. "There is no other way to enter to God except through his Son."

**75:4** And I saw — six young men came and stood beside the gate, and a great multitude of men came also to build the tower upon the rock. And the virgins who stood around the gate urged the men to haste to build the tower.

**75:5** The six young men who were beside the gate commanded the men who came to build the tower to carry the stones for the building. And the forty virgins carried the stones from the gate and gave them to the six young men, who received them and built.

**75:6** Those men who came who were strong carried the stones from the plain. Others received stones from some place that was hilly and brought them for the building. And the virgins carried them from the plain through the gate and gave them to the builders for the tower.

**75:7** And when the shining stones were brought that were cut from the plain, those men who carried them dressed them and gave them to the virgins, and the virgins carried them through the gate to the builders. And when the stones were placed in the building, they appeared just as when they had been cut, for they were so bright and shining.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the great rock, gate, and virgins vision of Similitude 9.*
